title: Gahadavala Dynasty
capsule: The Gahadavala dynasty ruled eastern Uttar Pradesh and parts of Bihar from the late eleventh century, with capitals at Varanasi and Kannauj, emerging as the dominant power in the Gangetic plain following the collapse of the Pratihara empire. The dynasty's greatest ruler, Govindachandra (r. c. 1114–1155), issued hundreds of copper-plate grants recording donations to temples and brahmanas across the region, effectively providing the best-documented picture of Gahadavala administration; his inscriptions claim suzerainty from Bengal to Rajasthan and from the Himalayas to the Vindhyas. The dynasty met its end at the Battle of Chandawar in 1194, where Sultan Muhammad of Ghor's forces killed Jayachandra, and remaining Gahadavala successors were extinguished by the Delhi Sultanate under Iltutmish by the 1220s–1230s.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory is well documented through copper-plate inscriptions, though exact boundaries beyond the main Gangetic heartland are approximate.
